title: Hold Settings for the Wound Care Supply Program
content:
# Hold settings — Wound Care Supply Program

Account operations settings governing holds on wound care programs, by tier.

| Tier | Inpatient hold required | Longest hold | Past-due age | Past-due amount that holds shipments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wound Care Self-Pay Program | No | 180 days | 15 days | USD 50.00 |
| Wound Care Commercial HMO Program | Yes | 60 days | 90 days | USD 75.00 |
| Wound Care Commercial PPO Program | Yes | 90 days | 90 days | USD 75.00 |
| Wound Care Medicare Advantage Program | Yes | 90 days | 120 days | USD 75.00 |
| Wound Care Original Medicare Program | Yes | 90 days | 120 days | USD 75.00 |
| Wound Care Medicaid Program | Yes | 60 days | 0 (never held for a past-due balance) | USD 75.00 |

## What each setting means

- **Inpatient hold required** — whether shipments must be held while the customer is an inpatient in a hospital or skilled nursing facility, because the payer does not pay home supplies during a covered stay.
- **Longest hold** — the longest time a program may remain on hold, in calendar days counted from the hold start date, before it is closed administratively.
- **Past-due age** — the age, in calendar days after its posting date, at which an unpaid patient-balance posting becomes past due for the shipment hold test; 0 means shipments are never held for a past-due balance on the tier.
- **Past-due amount that holds shipments** — the past-due amount, in USD, at or above which further shipments are held under the past-due rule.

## Notes

- The Wound Care Self-Pay Program is the only tier without an inpatient hold; it also has the longest hold (180 days) and the shortest past-due age (15 days).
- On the Wound Care Medicaid Program the past-due age is 0, so the USD 75.00 figure never comes into play there.
